title: Investigation lifecycle
summary: Read the runtime as a sequence of capabilities, operations, receipts, and one terminal transition.
audience: A contributor changing workspace, execution, receipt, artifact, or finalization behavior.

claims.text: The lifecycle model distinguishes materialized, active, and finalized investigations. The state parameter is proof carried by the value: execution consumes the active capability, while finalization ends those permissions.
A snapshot is part of the capability boundary rather than an incidental string. Writer operations advance it intentionally; readers state which snapshot they expect.

sections.heading: Every accepted invocation becomes terminal evidence

claims.text: Receipts form a closed outcome union: succeeded, failed, or cancelled. Callers can branch on the outcome without interpreting subprocess logs or guessing whether a retry already committed evidence.
Artifact references retain URI, media type, digest, byte count, and completeness. Promotion rechecks that retained evidence before bytes cross back into the repository.

sections.heading: The service owns transitions; tools own adaptation

claims.text: The investigation service is the application boundary. Tool descriptors bind a noun-specific request to that lifecycle, and the MCP server adapts the resulting operations to protocol calls.
